t: For procurement of aircraft, missiles, tracked combat vehicles, ammunition, other weapons, and other procurement for the reserve components of the Armed Forces; $777,000,000, to remain available for obligation until September 30, 1998: Provided, That the Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components shall, not later than 30 days after the enactment of this Act, individually submit to the congressional defense committees the modernization priority assessment for their respective Reserve or National Guard component.

fable.w: This is an appropriation for reserve component procurement with a proviso requiring federal military officials to submit an assessment to congressional defense committees. The tempting reading is that the submission of priority assessments by National Guard chiefs is a form of consultation, but both the submitters and the recipients (Congress) are inside the federal government. No outside party such as a state, the public, or experts is consulted before a federal decision.
fable.s: the Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components shall, not later than 30 days after the enactment of this Act, individually submit to the congressional defense committees the modernization priority assessment

opus.w: This section provides money for procurement and requires federal military component chiefs to submit assessments to the congressional defense committees. Reports to Congress or its committees stay inside the federal government. Calling the reserve chiefs outside parties would be wrong because they are federal officials, and no states, experts, or members of the public take part in any decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.
opus.s: the Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components shall, not later than 30 days after the enactment of this Act, individually submit to the congressional defense committees the modernization priority assessment for their respective Reserve or National Guard component.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components" might mean state National Guard officials who are outside the federal government. That reading fails: these Chiefs are federal military officials, and the only process described is a report to the congressional defense committees, which are part of Congress. Under the definition, that interaction stays inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires federal military officials (Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components) to submit reports to congressional committees. Both the submitters and the recipients are inside the federal government. There is no consultation, coordination, or participation involving parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities).
qwen_chat.s: the Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components shall, not later than 30 days after the enactment of this Act, individually submit to the congressional defense committees the modernization priority assessment for their respective Reserve or National Guard component.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard are submitting assessments to Congress, this involves external stakeholders. However, the Chiefs of the Reserve and National Guard components are federal military officers (inside the federal government), and Congress is also inside the federal government. Therefore, this is an internal government reporting requirement, not participation by outside parties.
